name: frankentui
description: High-performance terminal UI kernel in Rust across 20 crates: diff-based rendering, inline mode, RAII cleanup, 70+ widgets, resizable pane workspaces, a Bayesian intelligence layer, and in-tree web/WASM backends (WebGPU with canvas2d fallback). 45 interactive demo screens run in the browser. WIP.

latest_release.name: FrankenTUI v0.10.0
latest_release.body:
FrankenTUI 0.10.0 keeps slow views live and gets inline logs into scrollback. A frame that runs past its budget is now presented instead of dropped, so an application with a steadily slow `view()` no longer looks frozen ([#104](https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentui/issues/104)), and inline-mode log lines now reach the terminal's history under tmux, GNU screen and zellij, and survive resizes. All 17 library crates go from 0.9.0 to 0.10.0 on crates.io. This release has breaking API changes, listed under **Changed** in the CHANGELOG; read them before upgrading.

Highlights:

- A late frame is presented, not dropped (#104). The frame budget skips a frame before rendering only at `DegradationLevel::SkipFrame` with `allow_frame_skip`; `RenderBudget::exhausted()` remains an advisory signal.
- Inline log lines reach scrollback under multiplexers. `TerminalWriter` batches log lines and streams them above the UI, and with `agent_shell` under tmux, GNU screen and zellij every line now reaches history in every mode tested, against none in v0.9.0. Resizes during streaming no longer lose log lines or leak UI rows into history in the cases this release fixes; **Known issues** in the CHANGELOG lists the resize cases still open.
- PTY child mode for subprocesses (Unix): `ProcessSubscription::pty(true)` and `agent_shell --pty`. The child runs on a pseudo-terminal and leads a new session, and `ProcessControl::request_resize` sets the PTY size and sends SIGWINCH.
- Pixel mouse (SGR-Pixels), cell size from XTWINOPS, and DCS/APC terminal replies in the input parser.
- Hierarchical accessibility for `Tree`, and one focus owner per frame (`FocusManager::sync_to_frame`).
- Headless stepping and shadow-run comparison: `Program::new_headless` and its step functions, `shadow_frame` evidence rows with a buffer checksum, and `ftui_harness::ShadowRun::compare_recorded`. `cargo install ftui-harness` now also installs `shadow_compare`.
- The lockfile moved past RustSec advisories.

Breaking changes were found with cargo-semver-checks 0.51.0 against the published 0.9.0 crates, plus two it cannot see (`ActionMapper::map` and `terminal_output_lock`). The full list is under **Changed** in the CHANGELOG.

Release gate: in two test suites, timing- and PTY-sensitive tests failed on a heavily loaded build host. Each failing test then passed 5 of 5 times when re-run by itself on a second host (64 cores; load average 16–22, CPU 20–36 % busy):

- `ftui-runtime` with `--all-features`: 4069 of 4070 tests passed. The one failure was a reactive-binding propagation budget test, `bloodstream_database_to_terminal_roundtrip_is_delta_only` (9298 µs against its 4000 µs budget). It also missed its budget in the default-features run (5312 µs). The re-run used `--all-features`. `perf_telemetry_config_jsonl_budget`, a timing test that had failed in an earlier gate, passed.
- The workspace with `--all-features`: 7292 of 7296 tests passed (one, `inline_never_clears_screen`, took over 60 s and passed). Two latency budgets failed: `agent_shell_keystroke_dispatch_budget_under_100us` (p50 121.22 µs against 100 µs) and `plain_pty_flagship_journey_without_cpr` (keystroke-to-echo 104.53 ms against 50 ms). So did two PTY capture tests: `pty_capture_drop_does_not_block_when_background_process_keeps_pty_open` and `pty_capture_partial_reads_across_calls` ("expected first chunk"). All four had passed in every earlier gate. The only code change since the previous full gate, where they passed, is in `terminal_writer.rs`; `ftui-extras` reaches `ftui-runtime` only through `pty-capture`, and the two PTY capture tests don't call `TerminalWriter`.

Binaries: `ftui-demo-showcase` for Linux x86_64/aarch64 (glibc 2.28+), Linux x86_64 musl (static), macOS x86_64/arm64 and Windows x86_64. Each archive has a `.sha256` sidecar, and `SHA256SUMS` now covers all six archives, the musl one included. The Windows binary is cross-compiled with cargo-xwin 0.23.0 (MSVC CRT 14.44.17.14, Windows SDK 10.0.26100).
